Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details:
- What the test sets up
  - It builds a MySQL-style format, then customizes it to:
    - use a quote character: withQuote('"')
    - set a null placeholder: withNullString("NULL")
    - quote non-numeric values: withQuoteMode(QuoteMode.NON_NUMERIC)
  - It prints two fields: the literal string "NULL" and a Java null.
  - Expected output: "\"NULL\"\tNULL\n"
    - First field "NULL" is quoted (NON_NUMERIC applies).
    - Second field (null) should be emitted as the nullString literal, unquoted and unescaped.

- How the current code behaves
  - CSVPrinter.print(Object) converts null inputs into the configured nullString:
    - If value == null, strValue = format.getNullString() (or empty if nullString is not set).
    - It then calls the internal print(object, strValue, ...), passing the original object (which is null) and the resolved string value.
  - The internal print(Object, CharSequence, ...) chooses quoting/escaping based on the format:
    - If a quote character is set, it delegates to printAndQuote(object, value, ...).
    - Otherwise, if an escape character is set, it delegates to printAndEscape(value, ...).
  - In printAndQuote, the decision for QuoteMode.NON_NUMERIC is:
    - quote = !(object instanceof Number)
    - Since the original object is null (and not a Number), this evaluates to true, so the nullString is quoted.
    - Result: the second field becomes "NULL", not the required NULL.
  - In printAndEscape (the case when there is no quote char, e.g., default MYSQL), the method escapes any occurrence of the escape character itself. If the nullString contains the escape character (e.g., "\N" for MySQL dumps), it will be escaped to "\\N". This matches the reported issue: nullString is being escaped.

- Why this fails the test
  - The test requires that the configured nullString be emitted verbatim, i.e., without being quoted (even under NON_NUMERIC) and without being escaped.
  - The current implementation treats the nullString like any ordinary value when deciding quoting and escaping because it bases the decision on the original object (null) and always passes the nullString through the same quote/escape pipeline.

- Root cause
  - CSVPrinter does not special-case the configured nullString. It:
    - Uses the original object (null) to drive QuoteMode decisions, which forces quoting under NON_NUMERIC.
    - Passes the nullString through escaping, which doubles escape characters when no quote char is set (e.g., for "\N").
  - This contradicts the intended behavior (and the bug report) that the nullString should be written literally.

- Consequences observed
  - In this test with a quote char and NON_NUMERIC, the second field becomes "NULL" instead of NULL, causing the assertion to fail.
  - In MySQL dump scenarios with nullString set to "\N" and escape backslash, the value becomes "\\N", as described in the issue report.

In summary, the failure occurs because CSVPrinter applies standard quoting/escaping to the null placeholder string. The nullString should be emitted verbatim, bypassing quoting and escaping logic.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

CSVPrinter.print(java.lang.Object, java.lang.CharSequence, int, int)
CSVPrinter.printAndQuote(java.lang.Object, java.lang.CharSequence, int, int)
CSVPrinter.printAndEscape(java.lang.CharSequence, int, int)
